validated_results.title: Alcoholic beverages and risk of renal cell cancer.
validated_results.reason: Population-based case-control study investigating alcohol intake and renal cell cancer risk with fully adjusted odds ratios and confidence intervals.

sample_size.excerpt: A total of 855 cases and 1204 controls reported their alcohol consumption and were included in the analyses. The distributions according to age, cigarette smoking, BMI, education, hypertension, and diabetes among case and control subjects are shown in Table 1 .
sample_size.location: RESULTS, paragraph 1; total_n derived from reported group counts 855 + 1204 = 2059

cases.excerpt: Distribution characteristics of 855 renal cell cancer case and 1204 control subjects

effect_size.excerpt: Compared to non-drinkers, a total ethanol intake of >620 g month −1 was significantly related to a decreased risk of renal cell cancer (odds ratio (OR) 0.6, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.4–0.9; P -value for trend=0.03).

confidence_interval.excerpt: The multivariate OR for more than 650 g month −1 (approximately 21 g day −1 ) of ethanol compared to non-users of alcohol was 0.6 (95% CI 0.4–0.9).

p_value.excerpt: Although a statistically significant association was observed only for the >620 g month −1 category, there was a significant inverse trend ( P for trend=0.03).

design.excerpt: We carried out a population-based case–control study of men and women aged 20–79 years without previously diagnosed renal cell cancer

timing.excerpt: We carried out a population-based case–control study of men and women aged 20–79 years without previously diagnosed renal cell cancer (ICD-9 diagnosis code 189.0), born in Sweden or any other Nordic country and resident in Sweden between 1 January 1996 and 30 June 1998

continent.excerpt: We investigated the association of different types of alcoholic beverages and of total alcohol (ethanol) consumption with the risk of renal cell cancer in a large population-based case–control study in Sweden.

ethnicity.excerpt: born in Sweden or any other Nordic country and resident in Sweden between 1 January 1996 and 30 June 1998

exposure_measurement.excerpt: All case and control subjects received a self-administered questionnaire on personal and medical history, as well as dietary habits and alcohol consumption 5 years before study, disregarding recent changes.

gender.excerpt: Cases and controls were broadly similar in distribution by sex (59% male cases and 61% male controls)

smoking_status.excerpt: cigarette smoking (never smoked, smokers stratified as low (⩽16.7 pack-years) or high (>16.7 pack-years))

extraction.p_value_method: two-sided Wald test from effect and 95% CI on the log scale
extraction.ethnicity_supporting_text: born in Sweden or any other Nordic country and resident in Sweden between 1 January 1996 and 30 June 1998
